patterns.title: Duplicate webhook or job effects
patterns.signals: A retried webhook or redelivered job sends two notifications or creates duplicate records.
patterns.keywords: webhook job duplicate retry retries redelivery acknowledgement dedupe idempotency notification
patterns.mechanism: The same logical operation reaches effect creation more than once without an effective deduplication boundary.
patterns.experiment: In an isolated test replay one operation identity twice, including a lost acknowledgement after the first effect; inspect durable state and effect counts.
patterns.falsifies: A reliable trace shows distinct legitimate operation identities or exactly one effect for the replayed identity at every relevant boundary.
patterns.verification: Replay and concurrent delivery must preserve the intended effect count; check payload mismatch and failure after effect commit.
patterns.limits: At-least-once delivery is a candidate until actual transport and consumer paths are inspected; some repeated operations are legitimate.

patterns.title: Concurrent creation or overspending race
patterns.signals: Parallel requests pass an existence or balance check, then create duplicate rows or overdraw inventory.
patterns.keywords: parallel concurrent race overspend balance stock inventory constraint unique
patterns.mechanism: A read/check and subsequent mutation are not protected by the invariant-owning atomic boundary.
patterns.experiment: Pause two isolated requests immediately after the check, release both, and inspect final rows, balances and effect counts.
patterns.falsifies: All reachable writers enforce the invariant atomically and the forced overlap cannot violate it; missing overlap evidence is inconclusive.
patterns.verification: Verify controlled overlap, normal serial behavior and retry/error paths with the actual storage semantics.
patterns.limits: A lock or constraint is not automatically the right repair; identify isolation, scope, and every writer first.

patterns.title: Timeout after an operation committed
patterns.signals: A caller times out but payment, storage or another external effect has already succeeded; retry repeats it.
patterns.keywords: timeout payment charge paid committed reply cancellation cancel retry
patterns.mechanism: The caller loses the outcome after an effect commits and retries as if no effect occurred.
patterns.experiment: Inject a lost response after commit in isolation, reconcile using the operation identity, then retry and count effects.
patterns.falsifies: Reliable boundary evidence establishes that no effect committed and the operation stopped before effects were possible.
patterns.verification: Check unknown-outcome reconciliation, retry identity and success/error/cancel behavior without real external charges.
patterns.limits: Caller timeout alone establishes neither success nor failure; provider and operation-specific semantics must be verified.

patterns.title: Saved state but missing notification or event
patterns.signals: Database state commits but a downstream notification or job is missing after a crash.
patterns.keywords: commit publish event missing notification outbox crash acknowledgement queue event
patterns.mechanism: Durable state and event publication have a crash window with no adequate recovery mechanism.
patterns.experiment: In isolation stop execution between state commit and publish, restart, and check whether the intended event is recovered.
patterns.falsifies: The relevant state and pending event are durably recorded together and recovery delivers the event; investigate downstream consumption instead.
patterns.verification: Verify restart recovery, duplicate consumption handling and failed publication; check eventual delivery bounds.
patterns.limits: An after-commit callback alone does not prove crash-safe delivery; notification absence can also arise downstream.

patterns.title: Stale cache or replica disagrees with saved data
patterns.signals: A successful write is followed by an old value or different values from two endpoints.
patterns.keywords: stale cache replica replication lag outdated freshness invalidation endpoint disagreement
patterns.mechanism: A read uses a projection whose key, invalidation, update ordering or freshness differs from the authoritative state.
patterns.experiment: For one isolated write compare authoritative state with each read path and version; bypass one projection at a time.
patterns.falsifies: The wrong value is already present in authoritative state before projection, or bypassing the inspected projection preserves the failure.
patterns.verification: Check write/read paths, delayed updates, key scope, refresh behavior and the contractual freshness budget.
patterns.limits: Stale reads may be allowed; define the freshness contract and avoid clearing caches while also changing other variables.

patterns.title: One user sees another tenant data
patterns.signals: User A receives user B data from a query, cache entry or reused request state.
patterns.keywords: tenant user data leak isolation authorization scope singleton cache key
patterns.mechanism: Tenant or user identity is missing from a reachable query, shared-state lifetime or cache partition.
patterns.experiment: Use two isolated test tenants with distinguishable records; compare identities, scopes and values at query, cache and response boundaries.
patterns.falsifies: Observed foreign data originates from an explicitly authorized cross-tenant contract and all reachable boundaries preserve its intended scope.
patterns.verification: Verify two identities in alternating and overlapping requests, including cache hits and relevant privilege boundaries.
patterns.limits: Do not access real unrelated tenant data or weaken authorization; the suspected boundary must be proven.

patterns.title: Old records fail after migration
patterns.signals: New records work but old records contain nulls, obsolete status values or unsupported serialized shapes.
patterns.keywords: legacy migration old records null schema backfill serialized format
patterns.mechanism: Readers or writers assume a new shape before existing data and mixed deployed versions satisfy it.
patterns.experiment: Replay sanitized old and new shapes against the same runtime; compare failing fields and test partial migration with active writers.
patterns.falsifies: The same failure occurs on valid new data before persisted-shape differences are reached.
patterns.verification: Check old/new shapes, partial runs, resume, mixed-version consumers and data recovery independently of code repair.
patterns.limits: An old record is not necessarily corrupt; establish compatibility and migration contracts first.

patterns.title: Incorrect totals or rounding
patterns.signals: Totals differ from an independent calculation because rows repeat or units, precision or operation order differ.
patterns.keywords: total totals amount rounding precision decimal float money sum units join
patterns.mechanism: A calculation changes multiplicity, representation, units or rounding at a boundary.
patterns.experiment: Calculate an expected result independently from raw fixture data, then compare row multiplicity, units and intermediate values.
patterns.falsifies: The independent oracle agrees with intermediate and final values for the failing input; revisit the expected business rule.
patterns.verification: Check rounding boundaries, repeated rows, zero/negative values and representation across serialization.
patterns.limits: Do not assume floating point is the cause; joins and business-rule differences can produce the same symptom.

patterns.title: Dates shift at timezone or serialization boundaries
patterns.signals: A date moves by one day or timestamps change when crossing parsing, UTC and local-time boundaries.
patterns.keywords: date dates timezone utc local dst midnight parsing serialization
patterns.mechanism: A date-only value or instant is interpreted under different timezone or parsing contracts across boundaries.
patterns.experiment: Trace the raw value and type through parsing and serialization with fixtures around midnight and relevant offset or DST transitions.
patterns.falsifies: The value and its date/instant contract remain unchanged through every inspected boundary and the independent expected value agrees.
patterns.verification: Check date-only versus instant inputs, offsets and relevant calendar transitions against the declared contract.
patterns.limits: Timezone behavior is version and locale dependent; changing every value to UTC may break a date-only contract.

patterns.title: Client fails after response contract change
patterns.signals: An old client fails after a backend changes response fields, types, error codes or ordering.
patterns.keywords: client frontend response payload field type contract compatibility deployment consumer
patterns.mechanism: Producer and consumer use incompatible observable contracts during version skew or deployment.
patterns.experiment: Compare captured old/new sanitized payloads with both consumer versions and inspect the first violated expectation.
patterns.falsifies: Payloads satisfy the actual consumer contract and failure occurs before or outside the changed boundary.
patterns.verification: Check old/new consumers and formats, errors and deployment-order compatibility at real serialization boundaries.
patterns.limits: Tests and current behavior are not automatically authoritative; establish the promised contract before preserving or changing it.

patterns.title: Memory or handles grow across repeated work
patterns.signals: Memory grows after repeated requests or session reuse; listeners, connections or handles are retained.
patterns.keywords: memory heap leak retained retention listener handle connection resource growth
patterns.mechanism: A lifetime or cleanup path retains resources beyond intended ownership or leaves growth unbounded.
patterns.experiment: Compare equivalent repeated workloads after warmup; profile retained objects and count handles after success, error and cancellation.
patterns.falsifies: Resources stabilize within the workload contract and the measured growth is temporary allocation that is reclaimed.
patterns.verification: Verify bounded steady-state growth and success/error/cancel cleanup under comparable load.
patterns.limits: One memory snapshot does not establish a leak; caches, workload changes and allocator behavior are alternatives.

patterns.title: Slow endpoint as data or query count grows
patterns.signals: Latency grows with returned rows or repeated database queries; workload size differs between healthy and failing cases.
patterns.keywords: slow latency n1 n+1 query queries database index plan throughput
patterns.mechanism: Repeated boundary calls, query plans or data growth amplify work or waiting per operation.
patterns.experiment: For comparable fixtures measure query count and plans plus time spent in CPU, I/O, locks and queues; vary one workload dimension.
patterns.falsifies: Query work remains bounded and traced latency arises at a different resource or external wait boundary.
patterns.verification: Compare equivalent workloads and latency distributions while checking output correctness and error rates.
patterns.limits: Do not assume N+1 or add caching from latency alone; index use and waiting require actual traces/plans.

patterns.title: Flaky tests depend on order or residual state
patterns.signals: A test passes alone but fails after another test or with parallel execution, time or shared fixtures.
patterns.keywords: flaky test tests order isolation fixture clock random shared residual state flakiness
patterns.mechanism: A test depends on uncontrolled time, order or shared state that changes its preconditions.
patterns.experiment: Run the failing test alone and after a minimal predecessor sequence using controlled clocks and isolated data; preserve the failure signature.
patterns.falsifies: The same reliable failure occurs with equivalent isolated state and controlled ordering; investigate the application path or test oracle.
patterns.verification: Check isolated and sequence runs, cleanup and meaningful concurrency; avoid replacing the failing boundary with mocks.
patterns.limits: Random repetition alone does not localize a cause; a passing run is not proof that flakiness is fixed.

patterns.title: Works locally but fails after deployment
patterns.signals: The failing environment runs a different artifact, dependency, flag or effective configuration than the healthy environment.
patterns.keywords: production local deployment artifact build version config environment env flag works
patterns.mechanism: Different executing artifacts or effective runtime conditions change the failing path or its semantics.
patterns.experiment: Compare build identity, runtime versions and relevant effective configuration between healthy and failing executions before changing one variable.
patterns.falsifies: Equivalent artifacts and relevant conditions reach the same path but outcomes still differ; examine state, load and timing.
patterns.verification: Verify the repaired path under the actual relevant runtime conditions and separate deployment, migration and recovery work.
patterns.limits: Deployment correlation is not causal evidence; do not collect secrets or assume source files match running artifacts.

patterns.title: A fix introduces another symptom
patterns.signals: Fix A is followed by symptom B or repeated patches change symptoms without new causal evidence.
patterns.keywords: regression patch fixes chain second symptom coupling fix introduces
patterns.mechanism: A patch changes a shared invariant or exposes another path; the new symptom may also be independent.
patterns.experiment: Compare before/after in an isolated workspace with user changes preserved; trace both symptoms to the first differing invariant.
patterns.falsifies: The new symptom reproduces unchanged on the baseline without reaching the patch, suggesting a pre-existing or independent issue.
patterns.verification: Check original and newly reachable behavior plus affected callers; remove speculative changes without deleting user work.
patterns.limits: Temporal order alone does not prove regression; combine fixes only when a shared mechanism is supported.

patterns.title: Missing, null, empty and zero are conflated
patterns.signals: An optional value disappears, a zero is replaced by a default, or an empty field behaves as missing.
patterns.keywords: missing null empty zero false boolean truthiness optional default omission coercion
patterns.mechanism: A conversion or defaulting rule merges input states the contract distinguishes.
patterns.experiment: Trace absent, null, empty, zero and false fixtures separately through validation, mapping and serialization.
patterns.falsifies: All relevant distinct states survive the conversions correctly and failure occurs elsewhere.
patterns.verification: Verify each contractually distinct state and rejected inputs with an independent expected-value table.
patterns.limits: Some contracts intentionally normalize these states; establish their meaning before changing defaults.

patterns.title: Equivalent-looking text compares differently
patterns.signals: Visually identical identifiers fail lookup, names collide, or text is corrupted at an encoding boundary.
patterns.keywords: unicode normalization encoding utf8 characters text bytes casefold accent locale identifier mojibake
patterns.mechanism: Different encodings, normalization or case rules change identity across boundaries.
patterns.experiment: Compare code points and raw bytes for failing and healthy fixtures before and after each transformation.
patterns.falsifies: Representations and comparison rules agree at the failing boundary; inspect unrelated lookup state.
patterns.verification: Check composed/decomposed text, case-sensitive identities and serialization against the intended contract.
patterns.limits: Normalization can change valid identity semantics; do not normalize every field automatically.

patterns.title: Large values wrap, truncate or change sign
patterns.signals: A large identifier or count becomes negative, wraps, or loses precision after conversion.
patterns.keywords: integer overflow underflow signed unsigned truncation precision narrowing large boundary cast
patterns.mechanism: A numeric value exceeds a representation range or narrows across a conversion.
patterns.experiment: Replay values around the actual type boundaries and inspect exact values before and after casts or serialization.
patterns.falsifies: Values are representable and unchanged at every relevant conversion; inspect the producing arithmetic.
patterns.verification: Check minimum/maximum boundaries and large identifiers using the actual runtime and consumer types.
patterns.limits: Numeric ranges and overflow behavior depend on type and runtime; never assume a universal bit width.

patterns.title: Changing one object unexpectedly changes another
patterns.signals: Two objects share a mutable child, a copied record changes later, or an iterator sees mutations.
patterns.keywords: alias aliasing mutation shallow copy reference shared object mutable child snapshot
patterns.mechanism: A supposedly independent value aliases mutable state owned by another path.
patterns.experiment: Track object identities and writers, then compare shallow and isolated ownership in a controlled fixture.
patterns.falsifies: Values are independent at relevant ownership boundaries and the unexpected write has another source.
patterns.verification: Check mutation of nested values, delayed consumers and supported copy semantics.
patterns.limits: Copying every object may break identity contracts or performance; repair the actual ownership boundary.

patterns.title: Resource used after release or invalidation
patterns.signals: A callback accesses a closed connection, disposed object, freed buffer or expired borrowed reference.
patterns.keywords: use after free release disposed closed dangling lifetime callback buffer ownership crash
patterns.mechanism: A consumer outlives the resource owner or uses a resource after its lifetime ends.
patterns.experiment: Trace acquisition, ownership, callbacks and disposal; force the suspected lifecycle ordering in isolation.
patterns.falsifies: The resource remains valid under the actual lifetime contract for every observed consumer.
patterns.verification: Check normal completion, cancellation, error and late callbacks with supported diagnostics.
patterns.limits: A crash alone does not prove lifetime misuse; use actual runtime or native diagnostics when available.

patterns.title: Fresh session works but reused session fails
patterns.signals: The identical request fails only after prior work on a pooled connection or reused session.
patterns.keywords: session reuse reused pool pooled connection reset fresh warm history retained request state
patterns.mechanism: State intended for one operation survives into a later operation with different assumptions.
patterns.experiment: Compare fresh and reused sessions while replaying the minimal predecessor sequence and recording state resets.
patterns.falsifies: Equivalent fresh and reused state fail identically before any persistent session difference.
patterns.verification: Verify consecutive operations, cleanup after failures and session reuse without restarting between checks.
patterns.limits: A restart can hide the trigger without repairing the owner or reset logic.

patterns.title: Dependency used before initialization
patterns.signals: Startup intermittently uses an unset dependency or a callback fires before registration completes.
patterns.keywords: startup initialization initialized registration readiness init constructor dependency boot ordering
patterns.mechanism: A path becomes reachable before its required dependencies or lifecycle state are ready.
patterns.experiment: Record readiness transitions and force startup/callback ordering in an isolated boot sequence.
patterns.falsifies: Every prerequisite is established before the failing path becomes reachable.
patterns.verification: Check cold start, concurrent startup and initialization failure behavior.
patterns.limits: Adding arbitrary delays is not evidence of readiness or a repair of dependency ordering.

patterns.title: Cleanup hides the original failure
patterns.signals: A close, rollback or disposal exception replaces the earlier exception or skips another release.
patterns.keywords: cleanup finally disposal close rollback original exception suppressed masked failure
patterns.mechanism: Cleanup overwrites the initiating error or interrupts required release paths.
patterns.experiment: Inject distinct primary and cleanup failures in isolation, retaining both causes and resource state.
patterns.falsifies: The original cause is preserved and all required release paths execute despite cleanup errors.
patterns.verification: Check success, primary failure, cleanup failure and cancellation with resource counts.
patterns.limits: Error composition and disposal semantics differ by runtime; inspect the actual contract.

patterns.title: Caller returns before asynchronous work completes
patterns.signals: An async loop reports success before writes finish or background failures are never observed.
patterns.keywords: async await unawaited promise task future forEach parallel completion background deferred
patterns.mechanism: The parent reports completion without observing required child completion and failure.
patterns.experiment: Hold a child at a barrier, inspect whether the parent completes, then inject a child failure.
patterns.falsifies: The parent observes every required child outcome before reporting success.
patterns.verification: Check child completion, errors, cancellation and required result ordering.
patterns.limits: Detached work may be intentional; establish who owns completion and errors first.

patterns.title: Failure converted into success or a default value
patterns.signals: A failed operation returns an empty result or success because a handler drops the original error.
patterns.keywords: swallowed exception catch except fallback silent success default failure empty result
patterns.mechanism: An error path removes the failure signal required by its caller or substitutes an invalid default.
patterns.experiment: Inject a recognizable failure at the suspected boundary and follow its representation to the consumer.
patterns.falsifies: The consumer receives the promised failure signal and handles it according to contract.
patterns.verification: Check success and each relevant failure path, including effect state after partial completion.
patterns.limits: Fallbacks can be valid; demonstrate that the fallback violates the requested behavior.

patterns.title: Workflow enters an impossible or stuck state
patterns.signals: A status changes out of order, a completed action reopens, or a failed transition leaves work stuck.
patterns.keywords: state transition workflow status stuck terminal guard compensation reopen illegal event
patterns.mechanism: A reachable transition bypasses its state invariant or omits required recovery.
patterns.experiment: Replay the transition sequence with duplicates, late events and a failure between state and effect updates.
patterns.falsifies: Every reached transition is permitted and recovery completes within its promised conditions.
patterns.verification: Check permitted/rejected transitions, repeated events and failure recovery.
patterns.limits: State names alone do not define valid transitions; use the domain contract.

patterns.title: Pagination duplicates or skips records
patterns.signals: Adjacent pages overlap or miss rows when equal sort keys, updates or inserts occur.
patterns.keywords: pagination cursor page offset ordering sort duplicate skip records tie stable
patterns.mechanism: The pagination boundary lacks a stable ordering or cursor/snapshot contract.
patterns.experiment: Page through tied sort keys while applying controlled inserts and updates; compare IDs against the promised snapshot.
patterns.falsifies: Stable identity ordering and the contractually defined view cover each expected item exactly once.
patterns.verification: Check ties, first/last page, changed data and cursor encoding with an independent ID set.
patterns.limits: Some live feeds allow changes between pages; establish snapshot versus live-view expectations.

patterns.title: Loop or range misses an edge element
patterns.signals: The first or last element is missing, an empty range fails, or an inclusive bound is treated as exclusive.
patterns.keywords: off by one index bounds inclusive exclusive loop range empty first last array
patterns.mechanism: Range or index arithmetic differs from the intended boundary contract.
patterns.experiment: Use empty, singleton and exact-boundary fixtures, recording iteration indices and accessed elements.
patterns.falsifies: Every intended element and valid boundary is covered without invalid access.
patterns.verification: Check empty, one-element, maximum-length and boundary inputs using an independent expected set.
patterns.limits: A boundary symptom may come from filtering or pagination rather than index arithmetic.

patterns.title: Loop never advances toward completion
patterns.signals: A retry loop, parser or traversal repeats the same state or cycles indefinitely.
patterns.keywords: infinite loop hang termination progress cycle recursion visited retry parser advances
patterns.mechanism: A reachable iteration neither changes the progress measure nor exits under its stop condition.
patterns.experiment: Trace a bounded number of state transitions and inspect the progress measure for a minimal failing input.
patterns.falsifies: Each transition advances or exits under the intended invariant; inspect external waiting instead.
patterns.verification: Check empty input, cycles, invalid input and stop conditions with bounded execution.
patterns.limits: Slow progress is not nontermination; distinguish finite work and unavailable external dependencies.

patterns.title: Split or combined stream messages parse incorrectly
patterns.signals: A parser works for one read per message but fails when messages split across reads or arrive together.
patterns.keywords: stream framing partial chunk packet split fragmented coalesced message bytes parser buffer
patterns.mechanism: Transport reads are treated as complete application messages without correct framing and buffer state.
patterns.experiment: Feed the same byte sequence under varied chunk boundaries and combined frames, retaining the intended message contract.
patterns.falsifies: All legal chunkings produce identical frames and the error is introduced after framing.
patterns.verification: Check fragmentation, multiple frames, truncated EOF and bounded buffering.
patterns.limits: Use the actual protocol framing rules; not every transport has stream semantics.

patterns.title: Output is truncated after an incomplete write
patterns.signals: Only part of a file or network payload is written, or a success count is ignored.
patterns.keywords: short partial write send bytes length truncated output flush file io network
patterns.mechanism: The producer assumes one write consumed the whole buffer or ignores a failing completion.
patterns.experiment: Use an isolated writer returning short counts and errors; compare accepted bytes with expected output.
patterns.falsifies: Every completion count is handled correctly and the full output reaches the intended boundary.
patterns.verification: Check short writes, empty buffers, mid-write failures and flush/close semantics.
patterns.limits: Write contracts differ by API; verify whether partial counts are possible on the actual path.

patterns.title: Retries violate dependency limits or repeat unsafe work
patterns.signals: An external API is retried after a permanent rejection or ignoring its rate-limit contract.
patterns.keywords: retry retries external api rate limit quota backoff permanent transient status dependency
patterns.mechanism: Retry classification, identity or scheduling conflicts with the external operation contract.
patterns.experiment: Replay representative responses using test endpoints; inspect attempts, operation identity and promised retry timing.
patterns.falsifies: Retries comply with documented outcomes and limits while failure occurs at a different boundary.
patterns.verification: Check permanent/transient failures, retry exhaustion, unknown outcome and permitted recovery.
patterns.limits: Do not induce real rate limits or external effects; exact policy is provider and version dependent.

patterns.title: Native boundary disagrees on layout or ownership
patterns.signals: An FFI call corrupts values or crashes only on one architecture or library build.
patterns.keywords: ffi native abi alignment layout struct calling convention architecture symbol binding marshalling
patterns.mechanism: Caller and callee disagree on type layout, calling convention or resource ownership.
patterns.experiment: Compare actual symbols, type sizes/layouts and calling conventions against a minimal isolated native-boundary fixture.
patterns.falsifies: Boundary definitions and ownership agree and corruption is already present before the call.
patterns.verification: Check relevant builds/architectures, error returns and lifetime with supported diagnostics.
patterns.limits: Architecture correlation alone is not proof; compiler, artifact and data differences also matter.

patterns.title: Concurrent edits overwrite each other
patterns.signals: Two readers update the same value and one successful change disappears.
patterns.keywords: lost update overwrite concurrent edit version compare swap optimistic increment counter
patterns.mechanism: A stale read is written back without an effective conflict or atomic update boundary.
patterns.experiment: Pause two writers after reading the same version, then release both and inspect versions and final state.
patterns.falsifies: The actual boundary detects conflicts or atomically preserves both permitted updates.
patterns.verification: Check overlapping writers, retry behavior and conflict reporting using the real storage engine.
patterns.limits: Not all conflicting edits can be merged; establish conflict policy instead of assuming commutativity.

patterns.title: Operations wait on each other and stop progressing
patterns.signals: Two operations hold resources the other needs, or nested lock acquisition blocks completion.
patterns.keywords: deadlock lock ordering cycle wait mutex nested transaction thread synchronization
patterns.mechanism: The resource wait graph contains a cycle or an unresolvable self-dependency.
patterns.experiment: Capture resource ownership and waits, then force the suspected acquisition sequence in isolation.
patterns.falsifies: No wait cycle exists and a single external wait or finite contention explains the observed stall.
patterns.verification: Check acquisition ordering, failure release and forward progress under controlled overlap.
patterns.limits: Timeouts and slow contention are not automatically deadlocks; build the actual wait graph.

patterns.title: Older asynchronous result replaces newer state
patterns.signals: A delayed request or event overwrites a more recent result or sequence.
patterns.keywords: out order older newer response stale async event sequence monotonic version late update
patterns.mechanism: Completion order is used as logical freshness without an ordering or version invariant.
patterns.experiment: Force the older operation to finish after the newer one and inspect identities, versions and final state.
patterns.falsifies: The boundary preserves intended version order and late completions cannot overwrite newer state.
patterns.verification: Check reverse completion, repeated sequence values and cancelled work.
patterns.limits: Latest completion and latest logical operation may have different contracts.

patterns.title: Batch fails after some mutations succeed
patterns.signals: A multi-record operation reports failure while a subset remains updated; retry repeats earlier changes.
patterns.keywords: partial batch bulk transaction atomicity rollback subset multi record commit
patterns.mechanism: The logical batch crosses atomicity boundaries or lacks a defined partial-success recovery contract.
patterns.experiment: Inject a failure after a selected item and inspect all state/effects before and after a retry.
patterns.falsifies: The batch either rolls back fully or exposes recoverable partial success as promised.
patterns.verification: Check every relevant failure boundary, retry/resume behavior and existing partial data.
patterns.limits: Not every batch must be atomic; establish atomic versus per-item semantics first.

patterns.title: Acknowledged data disappears after restart
patterns.signals: A write reports success but data is missing after a crash, restart or failover.
patterns.keywords: durability durable acknowledged flush fsync restart crash failover persistent lost write
patterns.mechanism: The success boundary occurs before the required durability boundary or targets a different storage owner.
patterns.experiment: In disposable storage compare acknowledged state before and after a controlled restart using the actual durability configuration.
patterns.falsifies: Acknowledged state survives under the promised failure model and missing data is due to a later write or read path.
patterns.verification: Check acknowledgement semantics, durable identity and supported recovery behavior.
patterns.limits: Do not power-cycle or crash production; durability guarantees depend on storage and failure model.

patterns.title: Requests stall waiting for pooled resources
patterns.signals: Connection or worker acquisition waits grow while a pool reaches capacity.
patterns.keywords: pool exhaustion connection worker acquire wait queue capacity backpressure saturated
patterns.mechanism: Capacity or release behavior leaves work waiting without sufficient progress or admission control.
patterns.experiment: Measure held resources, waiters and release paths under a bounded equivalent workload with success/error/cancel cases.
patterns.falsifies: Capacity remains available and traced delay occurs after acquisition.
patterns.verification: Check progress, bounded queues, release behavior and success/error rates under comparable load.
patterns.limits: Increasing pool size can move the bottleneck or overload a downstream dependency.

patterns.title: Required tasks never receive execution time
patterns.signals: Timers or callbacks stop responding during CPU work or blocking operations on a shared scheduler.
patterns.keywords: scheduler starvation event loop blocking fairness thread cpu timer callback responsiveness
patterns.mechanism: Work occupies shared execution capacity so required tasks cannot make timely progress.
patterns.experiment: Measure runnable versus blocked work and callback delays while isolating the suspected blocking path.
patterns.falsifies: Execution capacity is available and delays arise from an external wait or queue before scheduling.
patterns.verification: Check responsiveness, throughput and correctness under a comparable workload.
patterns.limits: Scheduling models differ; do not infer event-loop behavior from a language name.

patterns.title: Work grows disproportionately with input
patterns.signals: Input doubling causes excessive comparisons, recursion, allocation or parsing work.
patterns.keywords: complexity quadratic exponential algorithm growth input size regex backtracking recursion workload
patterns.mechanism: The actual algorithm amplifies work faster than the workload contract permits.
patterns.experiment: Vary one input dimension in bounded fixtures and measure operation counts as well as elapsed time.
patterns.falsifies: Measured work scales within expected bounds and waits or resource limits explain latency.
patterns.verification: Check equivalent outputs, edge cases and resource bounds across representative input sizes.
patterns.limits: Small stopwatch samples do not establish complexity; preserve the same execution path.

patterns.title: Expected test result contradicts the contract
patterns.signals: Tests pass an incorrect formula or fail a valid change because expectations reuse implementation logic.
patterns.keywords: oracle expected expectation test tautology snapshot requirement specification independent formula
patterns.mechanism: The correctness detector encodes the wrong requirement or cannot distinguish the faulty behavior.
patterns.experiment: Derive expected behavior independently from the authoritative contract and compare it with test and implementation outputs.
patterns.falsifies: The independent contract supports the existing oracle and the implementation violates it.
patterns.verification: Check a failing example and meaningful counterexamples without weakening a correct safeguard.
patterns.limits: Ambiguous requirements require a decision; never rewrite expected values just to pass tests.

patterns.title: Mocks hide the failing integration semantics
patterns.signals: Unit tests pass while the real database, serializer or provider follows different behavior.
patterns.keywords: mock mocked stub fake integration transaction serializer provider semantics tests pass
patterns.mechanism: The substituted boundary omits the behavior that causes the real failure.
patterns.experiment: Replay a minimal failing path against the actual relevant boundary in an isolated environment and compare the substitute.
patterns.falsifies: The substitute preserves the relevant semantics and the divergence occurs elsewhere.
patterns.verification: Verify the mechanism at its real boundary and retain contained tests for unrelated effects.
patterns.limits: Removing every mock is unnecessary; only observe the boundary relevant to the failure.

patterns.title: Logging or debugging changes the failure
patterns.signals: A race or lazy-load error disappears when tracing, inspecting an object or attaching a debugger.
patterns.keywords: observer observation logging debugger instrumentation heisenbug lazy getter inspection timing
patterns.mechanism: Observation changes timing, evaluation, locking or lifetime needed by the failure.
patterns.experiment: Compare equivalent runs with bounded scalar observations and with the intrusive observer, recording path and overhead differences.
patterns.falsifies: The observer leaves relevant execution conditions unchanged and another controlled factor explains the difference.
patterns.verification: Verify the original uninstrumented path after repair and retain necessary evidence with stated limits.
patterns.limits: Disappearance while logging is not a repair and missing traces do not prove absence.

patterns.title: Trace points to source that is not executing
patterns.signals: A stack line, generated file or source map points at a different build than the failing binary.
patterns.keywords: source map sourcemap symbols debug generated artifact line stack binary build mismatch
patterns.mechanism: Source-to-artifact mapping is stale or resolves to a different generated/deployed implementation.
patterns.experiment: Match artifact hashes and debug/source-map identities, then verify one observed instruction or transformation against resolved source.
patterns.falsifies: The mapping matches the executing artifact at the failing boundary.
patterns.verification: Check the repaired artifact and its diagnostics, not merely edited source files.
patterns.limits: Do not infer runtime behavior solely from repository manifests or displayed line numbers.

patterns.title: An alternate path bypasses an access decision
patterns.signals: A protected action works through a secondary route or authorization is checked against the wrong resource.
patterns.keywords: authorization access permission role policy bypass route resource identity privilege denied allowed
patterns.mechanism: A reachable operation does not enforce its authorization contract at the invariant owner.
patterns.experiment: Using isolated identities and fixtures compare equivalent operations through each relevant entrypoint and inspect decision inputs.
patterns.falsifies: Every reached entrypoint enforces the intended resource and actor policy before effects.
patterns.verification: Check allowed and denied actors, alternate paths and side effects without weakening guards.
patterns.limits: This is a debugging prompt, not authorization for a broad security audit or real privilege escalation.

patterns.title: Validation and use interpret the same input differently
patterns.signals: A path or identifier passes validation but decoding or normalization changes its meaning before use.
patterns.keywords: canonicalization validation decode normalize path identifier traversal interpretation boundary
patterns.mechanism: Validation and the consuming boundary apply incompatible representations or trust rules.
patterns.experiment: Trace sanitized boundary fixtures through validation and use, including encoded and normalized equivalents in isolation.
patterns.falsifies: Validation evaluates the exact representation and authority used by the consuming boundary.
patterns.verification: Check accepted/rejected representations and intended resource scope at actual use.
patterns.limits: Do not weaken validation or test unauthorized resources; establish the consuming contract first.

patterns.title: Reused credential state applies to the wrong operation
patterns.signals: An expired or previous identity remains attached to a pooled client after credential refresh or sign-out.
patterns.keywords: credential token authentication expired refresh identity signout client scope reused session
patterns.mechanism: Credential lifecycle or scope is reused beyond its intended actor, audience or validity boundary.
patterns.experiment: Use disposable identities to trace effective actor/audience and refresh/sign-out transitions across reused clients.
patterns.falsifies: Every operation uses the intended valid identity and the rejection originates outside credential scope.
patterns.verification: Check refresh, expiry, identity switch and failed refresh without exposing credentials.
patterns.limits: Token validity is provider-specific; do not print secrets or change policy to suppress failures.
